name: Pannekoek
summary: Thin cinnamon-sugar pancakes: soft, lacy pancakes sprinkled with cinnamon sugar and lemon and rolled up while warm.
about: Pannekoek came to the Cape with Dutch settlers and became an Afrikaans favourite: thin, soft pancakes rolled with cinnamon sugar and a squeeze of lemon, made by the dozen at church bazaars and school fêtes and on rainy afternoons at home.

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil
ingredients.note: plus a little for the pan

steps: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a bowl.

Whisk the eggs, milk and water together, then whisk them gradually into the flour to a smooth, thin batter like pouring cream. Whisk in the oil. If you have time, rest it in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon. Set a plate over a pot of barely simmering water to keep the pancakes warm.
Heat a 20–22 cm non-stick pan over medium-high heat and brush it with a thin film of oil. Pour in about 80 ml of batter and swirl at once to coat the base thinly.
Cook for about 1 minute, until the edges lift and the underside is golden in patches, then flip and cook for 30 seconds more.
Slide onto the warm plate, sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and a squeeze of lemon, and roll up. Repeat with the rest of the batter, stacking the rolled pancakes, and serve warm.
prepNote: Make the batter up to a day ahead and keep it in the fridge; whisk before using.
